front: What is the core invariant of State Machine Replication?
back: Foundational paradigm for building fault-tolerant services by executing identical replica state machines across a distributed cluster. Ensures that any deterministic state machine starting from the same initial state and processing the exact same sequence of inputs will arrive at identical final states.
source_ref: Raft Consensus Invariants & Safety Proofs (notes), Page 4

front: What is the core invariant of Distributed Consensus Fundamentals?
back: Study of agreeing on values or execution sequences among a network of independent nodes susceptible to crash-stop or crash-fault failures. It establishes the theoretical limits of agreement under asynchronous network conditions.
source_ref: Raft Consensus Invariants & Safety Proofs (notes), Page 4

front: What is the core invariant of Classic Paxos Protocol?
back: Classic consensus algorithm designed by Leslie Lamport that achieves agreement in a network of unreliable processors. It operates through propose, promise, accept, and accepted phases to guarantee consensus safety.
source_ref: Raft Consensus Invariants & Safety Proofs (notes), Page 4

front: What is the core invariant of Raft Leader Election?
back: Decomposition of consensus into distinct sub-problems, beginning with electing a single authoritative leader to manage the replicated log. Utilizes randomized timeouts to prevent split votes during simultaneous candidate campaigns.
source_ref: Raft Consensus Invariants & Safety Proofs (notes), Page 4

front: What is the core invariant of Log Replication & AppendEntries?
back: Mechanism by which the elected leader accepts client commands, appends them to its local log, and issues AppendEntries RPCs to replicate them across followers. Enforces consistency checks to ensure follower logs align with the leader's log.
source_ref: Raft Consensus Invariants & Safety Proofs (notes), Page 4
